title: I’ve been working on a gothic card-based autobattler for three months made possible by Claude (even the game trailer)
author: Dreamt_Up_Games
selftext:
Middle-aged solo dev here. I love autobattlers like The Bazaar and Grail, but they're bright colours and cute themes, so I'm making a gothic one called Midnight Bell. You build a team of werewolves, vampires or monster hunters, and halfway through every fight the midnight bell rings and the monsters transform.

I use Claude Code for almost everything except deciding what the game should be. I write a brief for a batch of work, Claude builds it, and I playtest in the Unity Editor while it works.

How it's wired up:

\- Unity: Claude runs C# inside the open Editor via Unity CLI, so it can start test fights, run the test suite and screenshot the game itself instead of asking me what I'm seeing.  
\- Balance: every card lives in one spreadsheet. Bots play full runs against each other, and after every change Claude reruns them to check each faction still wins between 45 and 55% of the time. It’s so useful to have Claude run thousands of simulated battles in minutes but it doesn’t eliminate the need for playtesting done by humans. LLMs can’t tell if something is fun or feels right.  
\- Art: ComfyUI runs locally through an MCP. Claude writes the prompts for each card, makes two takes, and builds me a little page where I click the one I want, add notes and paste my picks back.  
\- Icons: generated in ComfyUI, then cleaned up in GIMP through its MCP so they all share the game's palette and ink outline.  
\- The trailer in this post: Claude recorded real fights straight from the game, cut them together with a Python script and ffmpeg, and mixed the game sounds under music I picked from a licensed pack. It took eleven versions, including one with a crackle in the audio that took a few rounds to track down.

What didn't work at first: Claude was confident in a way that cost me time. It would tell me a layout was centred when it was visibly off, or that a fix worked when it hadn't run it. Now it has to build and run things before it says they work, and measure a layout before it shows me a screenshot.

The art prompts had their own habits too. For a while every scene had a lantern in it. Characters kept ending up on piers next to lakes, and a run of animals all had bandaged legs. I keep a list of banned motifs in Claude's memory now, but it keeps finding new favourites.

What I still do myself: the game design, the final say on every card and every picture, and a lot of playtesting.

If you want to follow it, the Steam page is here. It comes out in Q2 2027:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/5476290/Midnight\_Bell/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=post&utm\_campaign=dev\_story&utm\_content=r\_claudeai

Appreciate the read! Next step: DEMO!
